items.title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference
items.desc: Presents CausalForge, an LLM-driven agentic pipeline that autonomously selects topics, formalizes statements, and constructs machine-checked proofs in causal inference using the Lean proof assistant, backed by a 7,035-declaration causal-inference library and a statement-audit step for human review. [arXiv econ.EM, posted 2026-07-24]

items.title: Unfit for stranding assessment: a panel-scale multimodal-LLM audit of building-decarbonisation disclosure (BeDA)
items.desc: Introduces BeDA, a multimodal large-language-model auditor applied to 2,246 firms (2003-2023), finding that only about one in five real-estate reports disclose operational carbon intensity per square metre and that European disclosure rates are roughly double those in the US, exposing a measurable reporting gap for climate-stranding regulation. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-24]

items.title: What A.I. Is Actually Doing to the Economy
items.desc: A New York Times 'The Daily' episode weighing how much artificial intelligence is genuinely reshaping jobs, productivity, and growth versus how much of the impact is still hype and anticipation. [NYT, posted 2026-07-27]

items.title: How Meta Got Everything It Wanted in a Secret Louisiana Data Center Deal
items.desc: An investigation into how Meta secured unusually favorable terms for a massive AI data center in Louisiana, illustrating the economics, subsidies, and local costs behind the race to build AI computing infrastructure. [NYT, posted 2026-07-27]

items.title: Chinese Chip Giant's Stock Soars 470% in Start of Trading, Amid A.I. Race
items.desc: Chinese memory-chip maker CXMT saw its shares jump 470% on its trading debut, a sign of investor appetite for AI-hardware plays and of the financial stakes in the US-China contest over AI chips. [NYT, posted 2026-07-27]

items.title: The U.S. Is Still Winning the A.I. Race. Trump Could Blow It.
items.desc: An opinion piece arguing that current US chip-export and trade policy risks eroding America's lead over China in artificial intelligence, with implications for competitiveness and industrial strategy. [NYT opinion, posted 2026-07-27]
